tagline: Around the Wallowas, with a look down into Hells Canyon.
intro: From Baker City, once the Queen City of the Mines, Route 86 heads east over sagebrush plateaus and the farms of Richland toward the Snake. Forest Road 39 swings north across the Imnaha and around the Wallowa Mountains to Joseph, and Route 82 runs west down the valley, up the Minam Grade and on to La Grande, 218 miles around.

Hells Canyon, off to the east, is the deepest river-cut gorge in North America. The Nez Perce say Coyote dug it with a big stick. Geologists credit the Snake River, at work for six million years and not finished yet.

moments.title: Halfway
moments.text: A town of 351, named for sitting halfway between Pine and the next settlement. For a year from December 1999 it went by Half.com, for $110,000 and twenty computers for the school.

moments.title: Hells Canyon Overlook
moments.text: Up a short spur off Forest Road 39, a paved overlook at 5,400 feet looks across McGraw Creek and the canyon to the Seven Devils Mountains on the Idaho line.

moments.title: Wallowa Lake
moments.text: A mile south of Joseph the lake lies between glacial moraines that climb more than 900 feet above the water, a standard example in the geology textbooks.

practical: Forest Road 39 is closed by snow from October 15 to May 15. Parts of the loop are narrow and winding, with stretches of more than eighty miles without gas, especially between Joseph and Halfway.
